label: sec:approach-to-exceptional-divisor
html:
Approach: from base M to fibre \mathcal{S}_p

In the QOU archimedean tuple (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}), the base manifold M carries the smooth metric in which two free vortices propagate. As the vortex cores approach a brane point p \in M, the smooth metric becomes degenerate. The base coordinate ratio z = \sqrt{q} - 1/\sqrt{q} drives the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p (state bundle fibre) into the foreground. "Below Planck scale" in QOU is a categorical statement, not a metric one. The relevant geometry switches from the base M to the fibre \mathcal{S}_p, where the morphisms are knot operators (knot-operator energy).

The encounter unfolds in three moments:

  1. Approach. Two vortex tubes propagate on M and approach a common brane point p. The Reeb flow on M tracks the motion.
  2. Crossing onto the fibre. At the threshold \partial F / \partial \mathbf{c} = 0 on the colour-tube cubic, the base coordinate z hits a discriminant zero. The smooth base structure pinches. The operative morphisms transition to those of \mathcal{S}_p — the \Phi_q-piece K_S (\Phi_q-piece).
  3. Merging of fundamental groups. The two vortex cores become parallel strands in a single braid. Their independent fundamental groups \pi_1(\nu_1) and \pi_1(\nu_2) amalgamate into the fundamental group \pi_1(U \setminus K) of the merged knot complement. Here U is a tubular neighbourhood of p, and K is the link formed by the two strands inside it.

After moment (3), the encounter constitutes a knot-theoretic problem. The merged complement admits a hyperbolic structure (Thurston relaxation). The SDP/LP machinery of Chapter 11 selects the lowest-energy link representative (SDP as thimble flow). Mostow rigidity (geometric confinement) makes the resulting topology—and hence the mass—discrete.
